we present a novel approach to jointly track multiple persons in a multi-camera setting.
we present a novel, two-stage approach to multi-person detection and joint tracking from overlapping cameras that outperforms state-of-the-art methods on challenging multi-camera datasets.
we present a novel, efficient and robust method for joint multi-person detection and track assignment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the joint estimation of person positions and track assignment can significantly improve tracking accuracy.

the joint multi-person detection and track assignment problem is well-suited for a two-stage solution: first, a tractable but approximate solution is computed using a subset of the available cues, and then, the full set of cues is exploited to re-rank the found solutions.
the combination of two steps (K-best hypothesis generation followed by re-ranking) allows for a more robust and accurate solution than either of the two steps alone.
